sources.authors: Lawrence F. Katz and Kevin M. Murphy
sources.title: Changes in Relative Wages, 1963–1987: Supply and Demand Factors
sources.source_parameter: Elasticity of substitution between college- and high-school-equivalent labor in a two-labor CES; inverse-demand slope equals minus its reciprocal.
sources.method: OLS log relative wage on log relative efficiency-unit labor supply and linear technology trend
sources.population: U.S. CPS, college versus high-school equivalents
sources.frequency: Annual observations 1963–1987; static conditional factor-demand elasticity

v6_values.transformation: Negate estimated slope; inverse of rounded sigma=1.41 gives .7092199

sources.transferability: Qualified skill-input proxy; V6 X=phi H excludes R&D labor and has varying augmentations and a markup wedge. Conflicts with current rho_US>1 restriction.

sources.title: Long-Run Substitutability Between More and Less Educated Workers: Evidence from U.S. States, 1950–1990
sources.locus: Table 4, p.656, panel B(iv), column 1; full panels A–C for estimator sensitivity
sources.source_parameter: CES long-run relative labor-demand elasticity between more- and less-educated efficiency units; schooling-law instruments mostly move the high-school-completion margin.
sources.method: 2SLS, LIML and Fuller LIML with state and year effects, schooling/child-labor-law instruments; preferred Fuller F=4
sources.population: 48 contiguous U.S. states, 240 observations; wages U.S.-born white full-time males40–50; supply white males21–59

v6_values.range_type: range of IV point estimates, not CI

sources.transferability: Qualified U.S. skill proxy; different schooling groups, long-run horizon, possible weak instruments, V6 R&D/markup/technology distinctions; not RoW evidence.

sources.authors: Francesco Caselli and Wilbur John Coleman II
sources.title: The World Technology Frontier
sources.source_parameter: Skill/unskilled elasticity 1/(1-s), where s is the within-labor CES exponent in a production function with physical capital.
sources.method: Development-accounting inversion of skill-specific efficiencies, conditional on borrowed elasticity and capital share
sources.frequency: Static cross-country levels, not an intertemporal parameter
sources.transferability: Useful normalization/conditional-calibration approach, no independent elasticity estimate and no direct V6 intermediate-input match.

sources.authors: Per Krusell, Lee E. Ohanian, José-Víctor Ríos-Rull and Giovanni L. Violante
sources.title: Capital-Skill Complementarity and Inequality: A Macroeconomic Analysis
sources.source_parameter: Nested-CES outer unskilled-vs-equipment/skilled labor elasticity, distinct from inner equipment-vs-skilled elasticity
sources.method: Two-step simulated pseudo-maximum likelihood, latent labor efficiencies
sources.population: U.S. CPS labor wages/quantities plus physical capital and quality-adjusted equipment prices

v6_values.transformation: Reciprocal of outer-nest elasticity only as analogy

sources.transferability: Outer-nest skill proxy is qualified; inverse of .67 would map the wrong input pair and must not be used to justify V6 complementarity.

sources.authors: Jan De Loecker, Jan Eeckhout and Gabriel Unger
sources.title: The Rise of Market Power and the Macroeconomic Implications
sources.locus: Author manuscript15Nov2019, abstract, equation7, Section3.1/Figure1 pp9–10
sources.source_parameter: Gross price/marginal-cost markup, then sales-weighted aggregate across firms
sources.method: Flexible-input output elasticity divided by input revenue share; sector/time production-function estimation
sources.population: U.S. listed Compustat firms, additional Census checks
sources.frequency: Annual1955–2016; inputs assumed flexible within year
sources.transferability: Exact reciprocal conditional on same marginal-cost object; low-to-medium economic transfer due to heterogeneity, aggregation, overhead, public-firm selection and time-varying empirical markups.

sources.title: Is Aggregate Market Power Increasing? Production Trends Using Financial Statements
sources.locus: Longer Time Horizons subsection/Figure5; Scite actual fulltext offset16000 contains numeric passage
sources.source_parameter: Gross price/marginal-cost markup based on operating expenses including SG&A as variable input
sources.method: Industry-specific Cobb–Douglas, two-stage production estimation; annual and three-year window checks
sources.population: U.S. Compustat domestic firms excluding utilities/financials
sources.transferability: Distinct cost-definition alternative to P5, not its sampling uncertainty; SG&A flexibility disputed, homogeneous V6 cost structure differs.

sources.authors: Jan De Loecker and Jan Eeckhout
sources.title: Global Market Power
sources.source_parameter: Sales-weighted firm gross markups in declared regions/countries
sources.method: Production method with U.S.-based output elasticities applied to global listed-firm accounts
sources.transferability: No direct RoW-ex-US aggregate. Headquarters is not production residence; selection/cost/technology caveats. Different US estimate from P5 remains separate.

sources.authors: Steve Bond, Arshia Hashemi, Greg Kaplan and Piotr Zoch
sources.title: Some Unpleasant Markup Arithmetic: Production Function Elasticities and Their Estimation from Production Data
sources.locus: Abstract verified; published-PDF direct fetch timed out
sources.source_parameter: Ratio estimator using output elasticity, not revenue elasticity
sources.transferability: Raises reasons not to treat production-based markups as directly observed parameters; does not itself give a V6 value.

sources.title: Comment on (Un)pleasant ... by Bond et al (2020)
sources.source_parameter: Output-elasticity markup ratio, with additional data/structure to address unobserved prices
sources.transferability: Retains disagreement around implementation; does not mean all true markups equal one.

sources.title: Micro Data and Macro Technology
sources.source_parameter: Aggregate physical capital-labor elasticity dln(K/L)/dln(w/r), including within-plant substitution and reallocation; no imposed stable aggregate CES
sources.method: Local-wage IV plant elasticities plus heterogeneity and aggregation; amenities/shift-share instruments
sources.transferability: Low: physical K vs total labor differs from V6 X=phiH vs unskilled L. Preserve complementary evidence separately from skill estimates.

sources.authors: Sebastian Gechert, Tomas Havranek, Zuzana Irsova and Dominika Kolcunova
sources.title: Measuring Capital-Labor Substitution: The Importance of Method Choices and Publication Bias
sources.source_parameter: Physical capital-labor elasticity, conditional on chosen synthetic-study methodological profile
sources.transferability: Low for V6 input margin. Baseline CI crosses zero and cannot yield bounded positive rho confidence interval by inversion; point3.33 only scenario analogy.

sources.authors: Tomas Havranek, Zuzana Irsova, Lubica Laslopova and Olesia Zeynalova
sources.title: Publication and Attenuation Biases in Measuring Skill Substitution
sources.source_parameter: Negative inverse skill substitution elasticity from wage-premium on relative-supply regressions
sources.method: Nonlinear publication-bias correction;attenuation/endogeneity comparison by estimator;Bayesian/frequentist model averaging;subjective best-practice estimates
sources.frequency: Mixed source frequencies;bestpractice favorsannualdisaggregatedpanel,multilevelCES,fixed effects and valid IV
